_about: Public procurement publishers that expose awards in the Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS) release or record format, so an award to a supplier can be stored as a FundsTransfer with the buyer as the funding party. One generic parser reads them all because the data schema is standard; what differs per publisher is the query API, described here as data. query_url is a template with {supplier} (URL-encoded supplier name) and optional {page}; a publisher is used only when enabled is true and query_url supports searching by supplier. Many OCDS publishers offer only bulk or date/ID paging, not supplier search, and some large economies (e.g. China) publish no open procurement data at all. A publisher with no supplier-search API can instead be ingested in bulk: set bulk_url to its full OCDS export (newline-delimited compiled releases, optionally gzipped) and bulk_format to "jsonl" or "jsonl.gz"; the collector downloads it once per day, streams it, and stores awards whose supplier matches the enumerated organization. Bulk ingestion is on-demand: a publisher's export is fetched only when an organization whose country matches the publisher's country field is seen, so a run touching no organizations from a country never downloads that country's export (set country to the publisher's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code). An organization's country is the country part of its jurisdiction, or, when jurisdiction is unset (common for foreign entities found via a regional registry), the registrant country from its RDAP contact evidence (a postal-address Location.Country, or failing that a registrant phone's country). A publisher is used in bulk mode when bulk_url is set, and in search mode when query_url contains {supplier}; a publisher offering both is searched (cheaper than a full scan). A publisher that publishes its own non-OCDS schema (e.g. Brazil's PNCP) needs a dedicated parser, not bulk mode. enabled is set true only after the query_url (or bulk_url) and the response envelope are validated against a real sample from that publisher (see the TED validation approach). Each entry cites the publisher's own documentation (ai-design-principles.md, principle 11). name is the canonical Organization name stored for the publisher's platform; country is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

publishers.name: Portal Nacional de Contratações Públicas
publishers.note: Brazil's national portal (PNCP) has an API but publishes its own schema, not OCDS releases, so neither supplier-search nor bulk mode applies without a dedicated PNCP parser; alternatively find a Brazilian publisher that exports OCDS.

publishers.name: Gobierno del Estado de Nuevo León (Contrataciones Abiertas)
publishers.note: Nuevo León state procurement — the current, maintained Mexican OCDS source (OCP registry pub/149; data through 2026, ~22k compiled releases, MXN). No supplier-search API, so ingested in bulk (re-downloaded daily). Validated against a real sample: buyer in buyer.name or parties[].roles, awards[].suppliers[].name, value.amount/currency. Other Mexican publishers on the registry (INAI national, QuiénEsQuién) are stale; swap bulk_url when a broader maintained export is found.

publishers.name: UK Find a Tender Service
publishers.note: UK national procurement (OCP registry pub/41; current, weekly, ~229 MB compiled releases, GBP). Ingested in bulk (re-downloaded daily). Validated against a real sample: award.value is usually empty and the amount is on contracts[].value (matched by awardID) or, for a single-award process, tender.value — the parser falls back in that order; many tender-only notices carry no award and are skipped.

publishers.name: Rwanda Public Procurement Authority (RPPA)
publishers.note: Rwanda national procurement (OCP registry pub/145; current, ~344 MB compiled releases, RWF). Ingested in bulk. Validated against a real sample: award.value carries the amount directly, buyer in buyer.name/parties roles, awards[].suppliers[].name.

publishers.name: República Dominicana — Dirección General de Contrataciones Públicas (DGCP)
publishers.note: Dominican Republic national procurement (OCP registry pub/22; current, ~424 MB compiled releases, DOP). Ingested in bulk. Validated against a real sample: award.value is empty and the amount is on contracts[].value (matched by awardID), which the parser falls back to; some releases carry no buyer party.

publishers.name: Honduras — Oficina Normativa de Contratación y Adquisiciones del Estado (ONCAE)
publishers.note: Honduras national procurement (OCP registry pub/122; current, ~301 MB compiled releases, HNL). Ingested in bulk. Validated against a real sample: award.value is empty and the amount is on contracts[].value (matched by awardID), which the parser falls back to; some releases carry no value and are skipped.

publishers.name: Paraguay — Dirección Nacional de Contrataciones Públicas (DNCP)
publishers.note: Paraguay national procurement (OCP registry pub/63; current, PYG). A flagship OCDS program, but the export is large (~1.7 GB), so the daily download and per-organization scan are heavy and may hit the scan line cap (incomplete); disable this entry if the cost is not worth it. Validated against a real sample: award.value carries the amount directly; tender-stage releases with no award are skipped.

publishers.name: Open Contracting India (CivicDataLab)
publishers.note: India's OCDS data is state-level (e.g. Himachal Pradesh, Assam) via CivicDataLab, largely bulk, so bulk mode fits: set bulk_url to a state export (newline-delimited compiled releases, gzipped) and enable after validating a sample.
